mainTopic: The end of פרק הערל on the אנדרוגינוס, and the opening משנה and גמרא of the new chapter on women permitted or forbidden to husband and יבם.
overview: The גמרא finishes a proof from the previous page. A teaching lists animals that cannot take part in תמורה, and the אנדרוגינוס is on that list, so רבי אליעזר does not treat it as a definite male. Next comes רבי אליעזר's ruling that one who has relations with an אנדרוגינוס gets סקילה as with a male. A ברייתא tells how רבי learned this one ruling at רבי אלעזר בן שמוע's study hall. פרק הערל then closes with the הדרן. A new chapter opens with a משנה about women who may be permitted or forbidden to their husband, to his brother the יבם, or to both. The משנה applies the same pattern to שניות, which are rabbinic bans, and contrasts the money rights of a שניה with those of women in Torah-forbidden marriages. The גמרא then asks why the first case says "married" and not "betrothed". It concludes that the wording matches the neighboring case of a חלל. Finally it asks why that case says "widow" and not "virgin", and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A teaching about animals that cannot become holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא continues a proof from the previous page. It quotes a teaching listing animals that 'do not become holy and do not make holy': cross-bred animals, a טרפה, a יוצא דופן, a טומטום, and an אנדרוגינוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cross-bred animals, a טרפה, an animal born by C-section, a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס do not become holy and do not make another animal holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of a proof that began on the previous page, and here it quotes the source text it is using. The next line will explain what this source means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is that the אנדרוגינוס is listed together with defective or unusual animals. If an אנדרוגינוס were simply a regular male, it would not belong in this list. The exact meaning of 'not holy' is still unclear, and שמואל clarifies it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal born from two different species mixed together
An animal with a fatal defect that will cause it to die within a year
An animal delivered through the side of the mother (C-section)
One whose sex organs are covered, so we cannot tell if it is male or female
One who has both male and female organs

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not start a new topic. It continues a proof from the previous page about how רבי אליעזר views an אנדרוגינוס.

phrases.english: Cross-bred animals, a tereifa, and one born through the side,
a tumtum and an androginus —
do not become holy and do not make holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכִּלְאַיִם וּטְרֵפָה וְיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן, טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof from the previous page about רבי אליעזר's view of an אנדרוגינוס.
steps.raayaObject: Whether an אנדרוגינוס counts as a definite male
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching listing animals that cannot become holy and cannot make another animal holy

steps.title: שמואל explains the rule and the גמרא concludes
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the rule is about תמורה: these animals cannot become holy as a substitute, and they cannot make another animal holy as a substitute for them. The גמרא concludes, 'learn from this.'
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: 'They do not become holy' means through תמורה. 'They do not make holy' means when someone makes a תמורה for them. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains that the source is speaking only about תמורה, and the גמרא then draws its conclusion from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל explains that the rule is about תמורה, in both directions: switching one of them in, or switching another animal in for one of them. Since the אנדרוגינוס is grouped with these animals, the גמרא learns that רבי אליעזר does not treat it as a definite male.

keyTerms.meaning: Trying to swap a consecrated animal for another animal, which makes the second animal holy too
Being the animal for which a substitute is made
Learn from this (the גמרא is drawing a conclusion)

steps.whatToRemember: An אנדרוגינוס is grouped with animals that cannot take part in תמורה, so it is not treated as a definite male.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
'They do not become holy' — through substitution.
phrases.notes: If someone tries to swap one of these animals in for a holy animal, it does not become holy.

phrases.english: 'And they do not make holy' — when a substitute is made for them.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source quoted in step 1 and draws the conclusion from it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since an אנדרוגינוס is grouped with animals excluded from תמורה, it is not treated as a definite male.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: an אנדרוגינוס is like a male for סקילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, where רבי אליעזר says that one who has relations with an אנדרוגינוס gets סקילה, just as with a male.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: One is liable to סקילה for him, as for a male.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the next line of the משנה to discuss it. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treats an אנדרוגינוס like a male for the sin of relations with a male, which carries the death penalty of סקילה. This fits the previous step: the אנדרוגינוס does not need to be a definite male for this law to apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Stoning, the most severe form of בית דין death penalty
Like a male
One is liable for him

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One is liable to stoning for him, as for a male.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the אנדרוגינוס mentioned in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו סְקִילָה כַּזָּכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, one who has relations with an אנדרוגינוס is liable to סקילה as with a male.

steps.title: רבי's story about learning from רבי אלעזר בן שמוע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that when רבי went to learn with רבי אלעזר בן שמוע, the students ganged up on him and let him learn only one thing: רבי אליעזר's ruling about the אנדרוגינוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי said, 'When I went to learn Torah with רבי אלעזר בן שמוע, his students ganged up on me like the roosters of בית בוקיא, and they let me learn only one thing in our משנה: רבי אליעזר says, one is liable to סקילה for an אנדרוגינוס as for a male.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a personal story from רבי. The one teaching he managed to learn was exactly the ruling of רבי אליעזר quoted in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students acted like aggressive roosters that do not let a newcomer stay among them, so רבי could not study there properly. The one teaching he did manage to learn in that study hall was רבי אליעזר's ruling that an אנדרוגינוס is treated like a male for סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
They ganged up against me
The roosters of בית בוקיא, which were known for being aggressive
Our משנה

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi said:
When I went to learn Torah
with Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua,
his students ganged up against me
like the roosters of Beit Bukya,
phrases.notes: These roosters were known for fighting off any newcomer who came among them.

phrases.english: and they did not let me learn
anything except one thing in our mishna —
Rabbi Eliezer says:
for an androginus one is liable
to stoning, as for a male.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי: כְּשֶׁהָלַכְתִּי לִלְמוֹד תּוֹרָה אֵצֶל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא with the story of how רבי received the ruling quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי received רבי אליעזר's ruling about the אנדרוגינוס from the study hall of רבי אלעזר בן שמוע.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how this ruling came down to רבי and into our משנה.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הערל
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the chapter: 'We will return to you, הערל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק הערל.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line that marks the end of the chapter called הערל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן shows our wish to come back and learn the chapter again. The next chapter begins with a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)
The uncircumcised one; the name of this chapter, taken from its first word

steps.whatToRemember: פרק הערל ends here with רבי אליעזר's ruling about the אנדרוגינוס.

phrases.english: We will return to you, HeArel

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.

steps.title: New chapter opens: four groups of women
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that a woman's status can differ between her husband and her יבם, and names four possible groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some women are permitted to their husbands but forbidden to their יבמין. Some are permitted to their יבמין but forbidden to their husbands. Some are permitted to both, and some are forbidden to both.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins. The משנה gives a short outline of four groups, and the lists that follow will fill in each group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a man may marry a woman depends on who he is. So the same woman can be fine for the husband but forbidden to his brother, or the other way around. The משנה lays out every combination before giving examples.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted, meaning allowed to marry or live with
Forbidden
Their husbands
Their יבמין, the husband's brothers who would do יבום

steps.whyThisMatters: This outline sets the plan for the whole משנה, which works through each group with examples.

phrases.english: There are women who are permitted to their husbands
and forbidden to their yevamin;
women permitted to their yevamin
and forbidden to their husbands;
women permitted to these and to those;
phrases.notes: "These and those" means both the husbands and the יבמין.

phrases.english: and women forbidden to these and to those.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter right after the הדרן in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman's permission to marry can differ between her husband and her יבם, which creates four groups.

steps.title: Women permitted to the husband but forbidden to the brother
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives four cases where the marriage was allowed, but the brother may not do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are permitted to their husbands and forbidden to their יבמין. A כהן הדיוט married a widow, and his brother is a כהן גדול. A חלל married a woman fit for a כהן, and his brother is a fit כהן. A ישראל married a בת ישראל, and his brother is a ממזר. A ממזר married a ממזרת, and his brother is a ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה fills in the first group with examples. In each case the husband was allowed to marry her, but his brother is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול may not marry any widow, though a regular כהן may. A woman who lives with a חלל becomes a חללה, who is forbidden to a fit כהן. A ממזר may marry only a ממזרת or similar, and a ישראל may not marry either of them.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
The High Priest, who may not marry a widow
A son of a כהן born from a marriage forbidden to a כהן; he lacks כהונה status
A child born from a forbidden relationship such as incest or adultery

steps.confusionAlert: How can one brother be a ממזר and the other a ישראל? For יבום, brothers count through the father. Brothers from different mothers can have different statuses.

phrases.english: And these are permitted to their husbands and forbidden to their yevamin:
A common priest who married a widow,
and he has a brother who is the High Priest;
a ḥalal who married a fit woman,
and he has a brother who is a fit priest;
an Israelite who married an Israelite woman,
and he has a brother who is a mamzer;
a mamzer who married a mamzeret,
and he has a brother who is an Israelite;
these are permitted to their husbands and forbidden to their yevamin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives examples for the first group named in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the husband's status allowed the marriage but the brother's status forbids her, she is permitted to the husband and forbidden to the יבם.

steps.title: Women permitted to the brother but forbidden to the husband
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives four reverse cases: the husband was forbidden to her, but his brother is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are permitted to their יבמין and forbidden to their husbands. A כהן גדול betrothed a widow, and his brother is a כהן הדיוט. A fit כהן married a חללה, and his brother is a חלל. A ישראל married a ממזרת, and his brother is a ממזר. A ממזר married a בת ישראל, and his brother is a ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה fills in the second group, which mirrors the first. Here the husband should not have married her, but his brother may do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules are the same as before, but the statuses are switched between husband and brother. In the כהן גדול case the משנה says only that he betrothed her. If he had lived with her, she would become a חללה and be forbidden to his כהן brother too.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothed, the first stage of marriage before living together
A woman disqualified from marrying a כהן
A widow

steps.whatToRemember: The two lists mirror each other. What matters is whether each man, husband or brother, is allowed to marry this woman given his own status.

phrases.english: And these are permitted to their yevamin and forbidden to their husbands:
A High Priest who betrothed a widow,
and he has a brother who is a common priest;
a fit priest who married a ḥalala,
and he has a brother who is a ḥalal;
an Israelite who married a mamzeret,
and he has a brother who is a mamzer;
a mamzer who married an Israelite woman,
and he has a brother who is an Israelite;
these are permitted to their yevamin and forbidden to their husbands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives examples for the second group from step 6, mirroring the cases in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the husband was forbidden to her but the brother's status allows her, she is permitted to the יבם and forbidden to the husband.

steps.title: Cases where she is forbidden to both husband and brother
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives four cases where the woman was forbidden to her husband and is also forbidden to his brother, the יבם. All other women are permitted to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: These women are forbidden to both: a כהן גדול who married a widow and has a brother who is a כהן גדול or a כהן הדיוט; a fit כהן who married a חללה and has a fit brother; a Jew who married a ממזרת and has a Jewish brother; a ממזר who married a Jewish woman and has a ממזר brother. They are forbidden to both the husbands and the brothers. All other women are permitted to their husbands and to their יבמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the third group: cases where the woman is forbidden to the husband and also to the brother. It closes with the fourth group, which covers everyone else, who is permitted to both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In most cases the brother has the same status as the husband, so the same Torah ban that made the marriage forbidden also blocks יבום. The brother who is a כהן הדיוט is forbidden for a different reason: living with the כהן גדול made her a חללה, who is forbidden to every כהן. The last line covers the normal case, where nothing blocks either the marriage or the יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest, who may not marry a widow
An ordinary כהן
A woman forbidden to a כהן because of a forbidden priestly union
A child born from a forbidden union, who may not marry an ordinary Jew

steps.whatToRemember: The four groups are: permitted to husband but forbidden to יבם, forbidden to husband but permitted to יבם, forbidden to both, and permitted to both (all other women).

phrases.english: And these are forbidden to these and to those:
phrases.notes: "These and those" means the husbands and the brothers (the יבמים).

phrases.english: A High Priest who married the widow,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ לוֹ אָח כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל; אוֹ כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
phrases.english: and he has a brother who is a High Priest or a common priest;
a fit priest who married a ḥalala,
and he has a fit brother;
an Israelite who married a ממזרת,
and he has an Israelite brother;
a ממזר who married an Israelite woman,
and he has a brother who is a ממזר —
they are forbidden to these and to those,
and all the rest of the women
are permitted to their husbands and to their יבמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third and fourth groups after the two groups listed in steps 7 and 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the brother shares the husband's status, she is forbidden to both. All other women are permitted to both.

steps.title: The same pattern for rabbinic secondary relatives
steps.stepSummary: The משנה applies the husband-versus-brother pattern to שניות, relatives forbidden by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: שניות, forbidden by the חכמים: if she is a שניה to the husband and not to the יבם, she is forbidden to the husband and permitted to the יבם. If she is a שניה to the יבם and not to the husband, she is forbidden to the יבם and permitted to the husband. If she is a שניה to both, she is forbidden to both.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now moves from Torah bans to rabbinic bans on secondary relatives. It shows that the same pattern of husband versus יבם applies to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A secondary relation is personal. The woman can be one man's secondary relative and not his brother's. So the ban follows whichever man she is related to.

keyTerms.meaning: Secondary relatives, forbidden in marriage by the Sages
Rabbinic law, from the Sages and not directly from the Torah
Husband

phrases.english: Secondary relatives, forbidden by the words of the Sages,
a secondary relative to the husband but not a secondary relative to the יבם —
she is forbidden to the husband and permitted to the יבם.
A secondary relative to the יבם but not a secondary relative to the husband —
she is forbidden to the יבם and permitted to the husband.
A secondary relative to this one and to that one —
she is forbidden to this one and to that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries the same structure over from Torah bans to rabbinic bans.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban of שניות applies only to the man she is related to: the husband, the יבם, or both.

steps.title: A woman married against a rabbinic ban loses her money rights
steps.stepSummary: A woman married to someone for whom she is a שניה loses her כתובה, payment for produce, support, and her worn items. The child is fit, and the husband is forced to divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: She has no כתובה, no payment for produce, no support, and no worn-out items. The child is fit, and the court forces him to divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us what happens with money and with the child when a man marries a woman forbidden to him as a שניה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She loses all four financial rights a wife normally has. The child has no flaw in lineage, because the ban is only rabbinic. The court still pushes the husband to end the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: The money a wife receives if divorced or widowed
Produce from her property that the husband used
Support and food
Worn-out remains of items she brought into the marriage
The court forces

phrases.english: She does not have a כתובה,
phrases.notes: "She" is the woman from the last step, married to a man for whom she is a שניה.

phrases.english: nor produce, nor support,
nor worn-out items.
And the child is fit,
and they force him to divorce her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the money and lineage results of a marriage to a שניה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שניה loses her כתובה, payment for produce, support, and her worn items. The child is fit, and the husband is forced to divorce her.

steps.title: Women forbidden by Torah law still get a כתובה
steps.stepSummary: Women married against Torah bans, such as a widow to a כהן גדול, still receive a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow married to a כהן גדול, a divorcée or a חלוצה married to an ordinary כהן, a ממזרת or a נתינה married to a Jew, and a Jewish woman married to a נתין or a ממזר all have a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה contrasts the last step. Women in Torah-forbidden marriages do keep their כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the surprising part. The Torah ban is more severe, yet these women keep the כתובה, while the שניה from the rabbinic ban loses it. The משנה states the rule here without giving a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorced woman, forbidden to any כהן
A woman released from יבום by חליצה, forbidden to a כהן
A descendant of the גבעונים, who may not marry an ordinary Jew

steps.whatToRemember: A rabbinic ban (שניות) means no כתובה. A Torah ban (such as a widow to a כהן גדול) still means she has a כתובה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the stricter Torah ban costs her more money. Here it is the reverse: the rabbinic שניה loses her כתובה, and the Torah-forbidden wife keeps it.

phrases.english: A widow married to a High Priest,
a divorcée or a חלוצה married to an ordinary priest,
a ממזרת or a נתינה married to an Israelite,
an Israelite woman married to a נתין or to a ממזר —
they all have a כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts step 11: Torah-forbidden wives keep their כתובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women married against Torah bans still receive their כתובה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This contrast between rabbinic and Torah bans sets up the later discussion of why the Sages were stricter in their own cases.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say married and not betrothed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why the first case of the משנה speaks of a כהן הדיוט who "married" the widow, when "betrothed" should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why does the משנה specifically say "married"? It should say "betrothed"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה's case of a כהן הדיוט who married a widow and has a brother who is a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow is forbidden to a כהן גדול even if his brother only betrothed her, because betrothal alone makes her a widow. So the word "married" seems to add a condition that is not needed. The גמרא wants to know why the משנה chose it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Why specifically this case?
Married, including living together after the wedding
Betrothed, the first stage of marriage
Let it teach, meaning it should have said

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Why specifically does it teach "married"?
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's first case: a כהן הדיוט who married a widow and has a brother who is a כהן גדול.

phrases.english: Let it teach "betrothed"!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא דְּתָנֵי נָשָׂא לִיתְנֵי קִידֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה cases summarized in earlier steps
steps.kashyaTarget: The word נשא in the first case of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Betrothal alone already makes her a widow who is forbidden to a כהן גדול, so "married" seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that marriage adds an extra command
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that "married" matters because marriage adds a עשה to the לא תעשה, and then rejects this from the rest of the chapter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: the reason it says "married" is that then there is both a עשה and a לא תעשה, but with betrothal the עשה of יבום would come and push aside the לא תעשה. But this whole chapter is about a עשה against a לא תעשה, and the עשה does not push aside the לא תעשה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to its own question and then shoots it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested answer: if she was only betrothed, the כהן גדול faces just one prohibition, so the מצוה of יבום could override it. Once she was married, there would be a עשה and a לא תעשה, which יבום cannot override. The rejection: throughout this chapter, a single לא תעשה is already enough to block יבום, so this cannot be the reason.

steps.title: The wording copies the last clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the first clause says "married" to match the last clause, where marriage really matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the תנא wants to teach in the last clause "a כהן גדול who married the widow," and there it must be "married," since that makes her a חללה. If he only betrothed her, she is permitted to his brother. So the תנא also wrote "married" in the first clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 13 by saying the first clause borrows its wording from the last clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last clause, a כהן גדול married a widow, and she is forbidden to his brother, a כהן הדיוט. That is only true once they lived together, because that is what turns her into a חללה. With betrothal alone, a כהן הדיוט may marry a widow, so the last clause needs "married," and the first clause copied it.

steps.title: Why not copy the middle clause instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the middle clause says "betrothed," so the first clause could just as easily have matched that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But instead of matching the last clause, let the first clause match the middle clause, which says: "a כהן גדול who betrothed the widow and has a brother who is a כהן הדיוט!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not use "married" everywhere, since the middle clause says "betrothed." So the wish to match wording does not explain why the first clause followed the last clause rather than the middle one.

steps.title: The wording matches the neighboring case of a חלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that "married" matches the very next case in the same list, חלל שנשא כשרה, where only marriage makes her forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because of the case right next to it. The תנא wants to teach "a חלל who married a fit woman," and there it must be "married," because that makes her a חללה. With betrothal alone, she is permitted. That is why the משנה says "married."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer to Step 13: the first case is worded to match the case right beside it in the same list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the next case, a חלל married a woman fit for כהונה, and his brother is a כשר כהן. Only living together with a חלל turns her into a חללה, so that case needs "married." The neighboring case in the same list matters more than a clause in a different list, so the first case copied it.

steps.title: Why say widow and not virgin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה's case of a כהן הדיוט with a כהן גדול brother describes the wife as an אלמנה, when it could have said a בתולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does the משנה specifically teach about a widow? Let it teach about a virgin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question on the wording of the same case. Why does the משנה say the כהן הדיוט married a widow, when a virgin would seem to work just as well?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's point is that the woman is permitted to her husband but forbidden to his brother, the כהן גדול. A כהן גדול may not marry a widow. So even if the כהן הדיוט married a virgin, once he dies she becomes his widow and is forbidden to the כהן גדול anyway. Saying 'widow' therefore seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? Asks why the text chose this detail over another

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי אִירְיָא דְּקָתָנֵי אַלְמָנָה? לִיתְנֵי בְּתוּלָה!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having settled why the משנה says 'married,' the גמרא turns to another detail in the same case: why the wife is described as a widow.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice of the word אלמנה in the case of the כהן הדיוט whose brother is a כהן גדול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The woman is forbidden to the כהן גדול because she will be the dead brother's widow. That is true no matter what she was before she married him. So a virgin would produce the same result, and the word 'widow' seems unneeded.
